Hey, I'm Konstantin
I've been in online marketing and performance marketing (ads etc) for over 11 years and helped scale e-com businesses to ad spends over $1m / month.

I'm interested in building tools that help businesses understand and optimise marketing and sales (think attribution, analytics etc).

Here are some things I've explored with AI:

- buildings dashboards tools for CRMs and third party, currently building a GoHighLevel tool with Augment Code- buildings reporting automizations (weekly ad reports, proposal builders)- prototyping apps ( Ice Bath & Sauna tracker) for fun

Here is why I joined:
Looking for a quality community to find the latest tech and support.
I just joined this community last night and... Wow, there is so much content here already. I feel like I'm a million miles behind you all.

Hi, I am Devon, I work as AI/ML and Cloud Security architect. I am interested in learning more about building full, end-to-end agent(Agentic) systems. I've explored multiple frameworks but my focused is on Pydantic-ai and LangGraph. Most of my coding has been around building tooling for work.

I joined because I saw a few of your videos and liked how you focused on building real processes for "AI Coding". That resonated with me, I'm working on a mult-agent system to guide "AI coders" through the full SDLC, from business analysis(refining ideas) to scrum master, to help them actually apply "AI/Vibe coding" in a meaningful way.

I joined because of the amazing value that Parker was giving on his YouTube videos 😄

Hey guys, I'm Davo with experience as a big data engineer and have done some machine learning prior to that.

I'm interested in learning how to leverage AI as a force multiplier to solve problems for people at scale so they pay me (Naval Ravikant - I see we're both fans, Parker) and ideally that I find more fulfillment in the problems I solve for people.

Here are some things I've explored with AI:
- All the models (hard to keep up)
- Building complex mobile apps with FlutterFlow
- Building websites, programs & exploring tools/mcps etc in Cursor/Windsurf/VS

Here is why I joined:
I pivoted into the data/AI space after studying mechanical engineering thinking probabilistically I would be well paid, be in high demand and have a long successful career. Now, with the rate of change of automation/AI, I'm worried about the future of work and primarily I just know my career isn't going to give me the time freedom & income I need to support my wider family (parents/sister) and truly enjoy life.

Hey, I'm Max

Here is why I joined:
I very much enjoyed Parker's youtube videos and am looking forward to learn from this community.

Hey, I’m Lachy. I’m a business intelligence consultant with experience across healthcare and the not‑for‑profit sector, and I moonlight helping run a beef farm in Tasmania, Australia.

I’m keen to learn more about:

- Whether my entry-level coding skills combined with the latest vibe tools are now good enough for me to finally complete some of the thought bubble side projects I've started over the years- Leveraging AI to bring more data to bear on real-world decisions we're facing on the farm
Things I’ve already played with:
[ol:1]- Most OpenAI models & tools- NotebookLM - I'm always listening to podcasts on the go, so having the ability to create them on-demand for reports & studies I'm reading has been invaluable. - Personal AI clone – an early prototype using ElevenLabs and Twilio that mirrors my communication style & voice (still looking for a good usecase to launch this on though)

Why I joined Parker Rex: To rub shoulders with builders who are a step ahead, get feedback on experiments, and gain motivation by being part of a linkminded community. Gotta thank the youtube algorithm for recommending me some of your dailyuploads channel vids - I connected with your communication style right away.
Looking forward to meeting everyone!

Hey, I'm Shawn
I am technical marketer for a lead gen company (also owner)
I'm interested in learning : coding with ai, building my own tools, automation
Here are some things I've explored with AI:
- built nearly an entire travel site for a pilgrimage trail in italy with chatGPT 3.5 beginning 2023

- learned and built bigquery database for lead gen quality scoring, reporting, etc- built 180 day email coaching program for one of our lead gen verticals

Here is why I joined:
My wife is our web dev, I am the gatherer. Meaning I see a lot of the trends and do, and sometimes I get overwhelmed and not sure how to start... because I want to do it "the right way" as fast as possible... so sometimes I get bogged down trying to set up foundation instead of doing. and other times i do and its a complete mess (e.g. the ugly and inconsistent field names on my databases before I understood how different systems talk to one another).

My wife and I are currently building a replacement for our web form builder (off the shelf service) because latency is hurting our CPAs. So we want to build our own. We've spent a couple of days working with o3 in the browser to build out our docs and specs, stack, etc. and I am still not convinced I have understood the best way to do things. I know to start with a prd, and I'm working on it... but what about all that other stuff...

So I randomly saw your youtube videos... and it looks like you got a lot going on. It also looks like you have reasoning and well thought out workflows. So I thought... i bet I could learn something. And hopefully get my project off the ground and start using it asap.

Thanks for having me

Good to hear it! The product strategy happens before you write code.

I follow a simplified format from the book [shape up](https://basecamp.com/shapeup) and have for close to a decade.

- Narrow the problem - Sketch out a few rough solutions to solve said problem - List things out of bounds (no goes)- List potential rabbit holes (things you know could be a time bomb) - Then time box it as a constraint (less relevant - never tell the ai a time box)

It works great for 0 -> 1 and for 1.0 to 1.1 and beyond.

I havent made videos about this ... but writing it out I realize I should

You get more leverage on your time writing code / designing if youve thought it out ahead of time.

And then you bring it into asking the AI how to further shape your idea, poke holes in it, find open questions, find where it fits into an existing codebase or where you should start if its brand new.

What HAS changed drastically is once youre in the editor...

because AI confidently paints a picture of how easy this implementation will be ...then its 4am and you're about to throw your laptop off a bridge.

So it requires having discipline around a set of steps you follow for all work.

If I spent an hour working on a new feature, I'd spend at least half that time refining the PRD. Taking that initial pitch format, doing research on tech / designs / other peoples repos I can learn from.

Then when I get to implementation, using a tool called Task Master, the majority of the intitial thinking is done. Which means the AI doesn't have to waste any valuable compute on it. Instead it plusses up and expands the idea, steel mans both sides.. and improves it.

From there you shape the idea further, actually guiding the AI to do the tasks. Making changes along the way...

And finally once you're happy with it you are now testing it locally.

A massive benefit of AI is making the 'testing' part of coding fun.

I rolled out a set of automations for my youtube videos that have 4 separate sets of tests. 4! I would've never done that without AI. Now its ready for any scale of traffic

Message me on Discord or on here and let's get your project off the ground. Need to know where you are at with it, and some other details.

Again happy to have you! Sorry for the long winded answer.

Hey, I’m Nicolas.
I’m a Product Manager at a no-code CRM SaaS company.

I’m here to learn:
[ol:1]- How to build fully-functioning apps- How to use AI to work smarter and empower the people around me

I've been using AI for the last few years but recently some things I’ve explored are:

- Used ChatGPT for deep data analysis — combing through cancellation reasons, support chats, and feature requests- Prototyped a field service management platform for work using v0 and bolt- Using Bolt.new in order to try to create a work Record Management System mobile app for firefighters (but then I got stuck) 

Why I joined:
Working at a no-code SaaS company, I’ve seen firsthand how many businesses spend tons of time and money on clunky, constrained custom solutions — just to keep things running. It’s clear to me that AI is about to flip that entire model. I want to learn how to harness AI in order to build tools that are far more valuable and accessible for the businesses that need them.

...also — hearing about your MAP product 🔥 — it’s the app I wish existed when I first started testing out different productivity apps.

Thanks for the warm welcome, that path from $0–$73M sounds incredible!

As for my experience building apps: I’ve been coding since high school, and during my electrical engineering degree, I worked with Java and C/C++. I also did an internship where I built a dashboard using Python and SQL to help online tutor managers make resourcing decisions in real-time.

At my current company, I started as a no-code “dev” using our in-house builder to create ready-to-use business workflows that integrate with QuickBooks. More recently, I built a PM dashboard in Airtable that centralizes key data like cancellations, reviews, support chats, and feature requests and lets us search and assign feedback to specific teams.

For the last build, I got stuck on OAuth, I think the Supabase rules it made were just a mess. I think it was just a matter of way too much way too fast. A dev at work showed me how much faster he was working with Cursor (like 100x faster!), so I can already see how having a deeper technical understanding would go a long way.

Just added the calendar call, looking forward to connecting more with everyone.

Here is why I joined:
I've been looking for an actual 'community' passively for a while as it's the best way to stay in the 'bubble' you want to learn whilst actually forming connection these days.

Parker's daily logs provide a tonne of value and I loved the emphasis of going full-stack and vibe-coding being the leverage. I knew I would gain a lot from the type of people gravitating towards this content.

I want to greatly improve my coding (particularly front-end) whilst monetising my skillset for cash-flow as I go along, ultimately building towards SAAS.

Building a brand is on my list also ofc.

Good to hear it! The product strategy happens before you write code.

I follow a simplified format from the book [shape up](https://basecamp.com/shapeup) and have for close to a decade.

- Narrow the problem - Sketch out a few rough solutions to solve said problem - List things out of bounds (no goes)- List potential rabbit holes (things you know could be a time bomb) - Then time box it as a constraint (less relevant - never tell the ai a time box)

It works great for 0 -> 1 and for 1.0 to 1.1 and beyond.

I havent made videos about this ... but writing it out I realize I should

You get more leverage on your time writing code / designing if youve thought it out ahead of time.

And then you bring it into asking the AI how to further shape your idea, poke holes in it, find open questions, find where it fits into an existing codebase or where you should start if its brand new.

What HAS changed drastically is once youre in the editor...

because AI confidently paints a picture of how easy this implementation will be ...then its 4am and you're about to throw your laptop off a bridge.

So it requires having discipline around a set of steps you follow for all work.

If I spent an hour working on a new feature, I'd spend at least half that time refining the PRD. Taking that initial pitch format, doing research on tech / designs / other peoples repos I can learn from.

Then when I get to implementation, using a tool called Task Master, the majority of the intitial thinking is done. Which means the AI doesn't have to waste any valuable compute on it. Instead it plusses up and expands the idea, steel mans both sides.. and improves it.

From there you shape the idea further, actually guiding the AI to do the tasks. Making changes along the way...

And finally once you're happy with it you are now testing it locally.

A massive benefit of AI is making the 'testing' part of coding fun.

I rolled out a set of automations for my youtube videos that have 4 separate sets of tests. 4! I would've never done that without AI. Now its ready for any scale of traffic

Message me on Discord or on here and let's get your project off the ground. Need to know where you are at with it, and some other details.

Again happy to have you! Sorry for the long winded answer.
